brief: Goldman's Coppersmith says AI sentiment has turned sharply negative over the past month. Tech was the most net-sold sector globally again this week, the US Info Tech long/short ratio hit its lowest level since 2016, and flows shifted from de-grossing toward new shorts, with NVDA seeing persistent long-only selling into hyperscalers. CTAs are near max short in NDX, so light positioning could spark a squeeze on positive news. Semis have underperformed the S&P by over 30 points since June, the sharpest drawdown since 2002. GS Research argues this has gone too far: the GS AI Semis basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus 16x for the S&P despite 31% consensus growth, implying an overdone selloff or priced-in earnings cuts. Clients' two worries are who funds AI spending and whether enough data centers can be built, a concern sharpened post-election by construction limits in states like Texas, though GS expects 2028 capacity to roughly match 2027. Financing is the bigger risk: borrowing costs are rising as AI firms need more capital, and new NVDA-sized deals may be harder to arrange than existing ones. Coppersmith still expects equities to grind higher after the reset but favors selectivity and disciplined hedges into NVDA's earnings next week.
